items.stem: Give an example of a flower which contains both stamens and carpels.
items.answer: Such flowers are called bisexual flowers. Examples: flowers of Mustard, Hibiscus (China rose).

items.stem: What is parthenogenesis?
items.answer: Parthenogenesis is the development of an organism from a haploid egg without fertilisation.

items.stem: What is DNA?
items.answer: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a double stranded genetic molecule which carries genetic information from one generation to another. Each strand is made up of many nucleotide units, while both strands are attached by hydrogen bonds.
items.ocr: Printed year tag truncated by OCR as 'Delhi 201'; read as Delhi 2011.

items.stem: Give an example of organism where binary fission takes place.
Name an organism in which multiple fission takes place.
What happens when a Planaria gets cut into two pieces?
items.answer: Each piece grows into a complete organism through regeneration.

items.stem: Name three methods by which plant reproduces by stems.

Name the part of Bryophyllum where the buds are produced for vegetative propagation.
items.answer: On the stems as well as the leaves of the Bryophyllum plant.

items.stem: Name two STDs.
What is the function of sepals?
items.answer: Sepals protect the immature reproductive organs of the flower in their bud stage.

items.answer: Male gametes: in pollen grains. Female gametes: in the embryo sac of the ovule of the ovary.

items.stem: Name the male and female gonads in human beings.
items.answer: Male gonad: Testis. Female gonad: Ovary.

Name the male and female gametes in animals.
items.answer: Male gamete: sperm. Female gamete: egg (ovum).

items.stem: What happens when vas deferens gets blocked?
items.answer: Sperms will not pass down from the testis to the semen.

items.stem: What is the function of petals?
items.answer: Petals are usually colourful and help in the insect pollination of plants by attracting insects.

items.stem: What is the function of DNA?
items.answer: DNA is the genetic material which is the information source of the whole body design for making proteins.

items.stem: How do different organisms get different body designs?
items.answer: Different adaptations and proteins eventually lead to different body designs due to variations in their DNA.

items.stem: Where is DNA found in a cell?
items.answer: In the nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplast.

Name the process by which organisms produce new young ones.
How do unicellular organisms reproduce?
items.answer: Unicellular organisms reproduce by asexual reproduction, such as fission in bacteria.

items.stem: Name a few plants which reproduce by layering.
items.answer: Hibiscus, jasmine, guava and lemon, etc.

items.stem: What is the product of fertilisation?
Name the agents that help in cross-pollination.
How is AIDS prevented?
items.answer: AIDS can be prevented by using a condom during sexual contact.

items.stem: An organism produces two different gametes which fuse to form a new individual. What do you call this type of reproduction?
Why do organisms reproduce?
items.answer: Reproduction is necessary to ensure the existence of any species by producing young ones.

items.answer: Reproduction at its most basic level involves making copies of the blueprint of body design, known as DNA, from parent to child.

items.stem: What is the expanded form of AIDS?
How do we know that two different organisms belong to the same species?
items.answer: A species is a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.

items.stem: By which part does Bryophyllum reproduce?
items.answer: By vegetative buds present on the leaves.

items.stem: Where is the embryo sac present in the flower?
items.answer: The embryo sac is present in the ovule of the ovary.

items.stem: What is the primary sex organ in the human female?
Explain how organisms create an exact copy of themselves.
items.answer: Through asexual reproduction, in which a single organism reproduces an exact copy of itself, known as a clone.

items.stem: Why cannot fertilisation take place in flowers if pollination does not occur?
items.answer: If pollination does not occur, the male gamete is not available to the female part of the flower, hence fertilisation (fusion of the haploid male and female gametes) will not take place.
items.ocr: Answer printed 'fission of haploid male and female gametes'; repaired to 'fusion'.

items.stem: Out of the following plants, which two plants are reproduced by vegetative propagation? Jasmine, Wheat, Mustard, Banana
Leaves of Bryophyllum fallen on the ground produce new plants. Why?
items.answer: Bryophyllum bears adventitious buds in the notches along the leaf margin. When the buds fall on the soil they develop into new plants under favourable conditions.

items.stem: State in brief two functions of Copper-T used by some women.
items.answer: Copper-T prevents implantation of the embryo and hence prevents pregnancy. It is a long term (5-10 years) contraceptive method.

items.stem: List any two reasons for adopting contraceptive methods.
items.answer: (i) Population control. (ii) To prevent unwanted pregnancies.
